text: Kitchen-table theme, warm cream. DATE: TODAY. REASON: -1. A tall paper fridge cutout stands centre, door shut. A paper hand reaches round to its back, low down. At "It's warm.", soft red heat lines rise off the coils at the back.

The fridge becomes a cutaway: frosty blue inside, a milk bottle on a shelf, a small thermometer reading cold (blue). Red heat arrows run from the milk, through the cabinet, out of the back coils and into the kitchen. At "It moves heat.", the label HEAT lands on the arrow.

The fridge LIFTS off. Navy night. DATE: BEFORE 1755. At "carried down from a mountain", a snowy peak and a basket of snow sliding down its side. At "caught on a winter night", a thin sheet of ice forms on a shallow dish under stars. At "from nothing", both LIFT off, leaving an empty workbench.
PAUSE 2s

Cream. DATE: TODAY. REASON: -1. Serif headline card, one italic red word: "How do you *make* cold?". At "a hole in the sky", a small paper Earth appears under it with a thin dark gap cut in the paper sky above it.

The headline LIFTS off. Five large icons appear along a dotted line, one on each name, while the matching icon in the top-right bar lights with its label: THE ICE, THE TRICK, THE LOOP, THE POISON, THE SKY. Then the big icons shrink up into the bar; REASON returns to -1.

Navy night. DATE: IRAN, 1600s. REASON: 0. A flat paper map of Iran slides in; the central desert shaded sand; pin YAZD pops in. At "forty degrees", a paper thermometer beside the map climbs to about 40 °C, past a small tick marked "HIGH FEVER 39 °C".

The map LIFTS off. Side view under a starry navy sky: a long shallow pool on the ground, a tall wall along its south side. A low winter sun sits behind the wall and the pool lies in its shadow. At "underground channel", water trickles in from a qanat: a dashed tunnel with a row of well shafts above it. At "as deep as your hand is wide", a paper hand measures the water.

Soft heat arrows rise from the water straight up, past the stars, to a label SPACE at the top of the frame. A small air thermometer beside the pool stays just above zero, label "AIR: ABOVE 0 °C". At "freeze", ice crystals spread across the pool. At "layer on layer", new thin layers stack up night after night (the stars wheel, three times), until a label reads "≈ 50 CM".

The ice is cut into blocks that slide into a cross-section of a yakhchāl: a deep pit under a tall stepped mud-brick dome, a small paper figure beside it for scale, label "UP TO ≈ 18 M". At "an ice pit", the word YAKHCHĀL · "ICE PIT" appears under it. At "lasted into summer", DATE changes to SUMMER and one block leaves on a paper cart.

Cream. DATE: ANY TIME. REASON: 0. The dome from 2a, small, dimmed at left. A paper hill fills the frame: HOT (red) at the top, COLD (blue) at the bottom. At "runs downhill", a red ball labelled HEAT rolls from HOT down to COLD. At "A cup of tea", a steaming mug sits in a cold blue room; its steam thins. At "It never warms itself", a reverse arrow (room to mug) appears and is crossed out.
The mug LIFTS off. A paper hand pushes the HEAT ball back UP the hill; a label WORK appears on the hand. At "Remember that.", the ball holds at the top. Calm hold.
PAUSE 2s

Cream. DATE: GLASGOW, 1755. REASON: 1. Portrait: William Cullen, plate WILLIAM CULLEN · PROFESSOR OF MEDICINE, credit WELLCOME COLLECTION · CC BY 4.0. At "A thermometer", a thermometer dips into a small dish of spirit and lifts out; at "got colder", its red column drops.

The portrait LIFTS off. A paper swimmer steps out of a pool into the wind; small droplets lift off the skin as pale puffs, each carrying a little red heat arrow away. At "five times the heat", five small kettles (freezing to boiling) line up against one gram-sized droplet.

The swimmer LIFTS off. A paper air pump beside a glass jar on a plate. Inside the jar, a small vessel labelled ETHER sits in a dish of water. At "pumped the air out", the pump handle strokes and small air dots leave the jar.

Side panel: a paper Everest with a kettle on its summit, a thermometer at 70 °C, a limp cup of tea. At "In Cullen's jar", the panel LIFTS off; the ether boils hard (pale puffs), red heat arrows run from the water into the ether.

Ice crystals spread through the dish and a white crust grows round the ether vessel. A paper quote card slides in: "we found the most part of the water frozen, and the vessel containing the aether surrounded with a thick and firm crust of ice." Source line: W. CULLEN, ESSAYS AND OBSERVATIONS, 1756.
PAUSE 2s

The quote card LIFTS off. The jar again: the ether level drops; its vapour puffs leave through the pump and drift off screen; a small label LOST. At "keep pouring in more", a paper bottle tips more ether in; the level drops again.
The jar slides onto a paper shelf. At "eighteen-oh-five", a ruler runs 1755 → 1805 with a faint pencil sketch of a machine at 1805 (label: DESCRIBED, NEVER BUILT); it then extends to 1834. Calm hold.

Cream. DATE: ENGLAND, 1834. REASON: 2. Portrait: Jacob Perkins, plate JACOB PERKINS · AMERICAN INVENTOR. A small patent scroll beside it: "PATENT No. 6662 · 1834". At "Catch the vapour", the Cullen jar from 3b returns small; its escaping puffs are caught by a pipe that bends round into a closed ring.

Portrait and scroll LIFT off. A large paper diagram: a cabinet outline (left) and a closed loop of pipe running inside it and out of its back. The four parts appear ONE AT A TIME on their words in the next paragraphs; until then the pipe is empty. Keep the heat/cold colour code.
The EVAPORATOR coil inside the cabinet lights, label EVAPORATOR. Blue drops boil into pale puffs; red heat arrows flow from a milk bottle into the coil.

The COMPRESSOR (a paper piston in a cylinder, under the cabinet) appears, label COMPRESSOR. The piston pushes; the pale puffs crowd together and turn red. At "a bicycle pump", a small bicycle pump cutout beside it, its end glowing red.
The CONDENSER coil on the back of the cabinet appears, label CONDENSER. Red heat arrows flow out of it into the kitchen side of the frame; red puffs shrink back into drops.

A narrow tube between condenser and evaporator, label EXPANSION. Drops squeeze through it one by one and turn blue; a small pressure gauge needle drops. Then the whole loop runs: drops and puffs circulate continuously.
The paper hill from 2b slides in small at the top-right of the diagram; the compressor's piston pushes the HEAT ball up it, label WORK. The loop keeps running. Calm hold.

Kitchen-table theme. DATE: TODAY. REASON: 2. The paper fridge from 1a slides back in; the loop from 4a is drawn faintly inside it. The back coils glow; red heat lines rise. Two small labels stack beside them: HEAT FROM YOUR FOOD, then (at "plus the work of the pump") + WORK OF THE PUMP.
The fridge LIFTS off. Cream. DATE: 1835. A paper model machine (pipes, a hand crank, a small box) labelled HAGUE'S MODEL · 1835. At "nobody bought one", a plain mono label NO BUYERS appears under it.

The model LIFTS off. At "eighteen-fifties", DATE: 1850s and a small paper ice machine gets a SOLD tag. At "The trouble was", theme flips to navy, DATE: 1870s, REASON: 3. Three paper bottles land one per name: AMMONIA, SULFUR DIOXIDE, METHYL CHLORIDE. At "all three were poison", a small skull label lands on each bottle, left to right. Calm hold to the end.
PAUSE 2s
